classification.difficultyReason: Choose suitable graph comparisons or polynomial graphs, then count distinct intersections or zeroes across cubic and quartic cases, checking that turning points near the axis do not create additional solutions; technology is explicitly permitted.

content.prompt: Determine the number of solutions to the following equations by drawing appropriate sketches or using technology.

answer.worked: Sketch $y=x(x^2-1)$ and $y=1$. The horizontal line is above both turning points of the cubic, so it intersects the cubic once. There is $1$ solution.

spec.description: Cubic and horizontal line with one intersection.
spec.mathematics: Blue y=x³-x and red y=1. Cubic turning heights are ±2/(3sqrt(3)), both below y=1.

answer.worked: Sketch $y=(x-1)(x^2+1)$ and $y=1$. The cubic rises throughout and intersects the horizontal line once. There is $1$ solution.

spec.description: Increasing cubic and horizontal line with one intersection.

answer.worked: Sketch $y=x^3-x+1$. Both turning points are above the $x$-axis. The graph crosses the axis once, at a negative value of $x$, so there is $1$ solution.

spec.description: Cubic with one negative x-intercept and both turning points above the axis.

answer.worked: Sketch $y=x^3+2x-3$. The graph rises throughout and crosses the $x$-axis once, at $x=1$. There is $1$ solution.

spec.description: Increasing cubic with its sole zero marked at x=1.

answer.worked: Sketch $y=x^3-x^2-2$. Both turning points lie below the $x$-axis. The graph crosses the axis once on its right-hand branch, giving $1$ solution.

spec.description: Cubic with two turning points below the axis and a single positive zero.

answer.worked: Sketch $y=x^4-x+1$. Its minimum lies above the $x$-axis, so the graph has no $x$-intercepts. There are $0$ solutions.

spec.description: Quartic entirely above the horizontal axis, with both ends rising.
spec.mathematics: y=x⁴-x+1 has its positive minimum at x=4^(-1/3), with minimum 1-3/(4 cuberoot(4)).
